address_spaces.name: I/O
address_spaces.notes: Sixteen small windows of 16 MB fill offsets 0x0000_0000 to 0x0fff_ffff, widget N at N times 16 MB. Seven big windows of 512 MB start at 0x2000_0000. Small window 0 and big window 6 are two views of the same widget, and both decode: Linux reads widget 0's identification register through the small window by its raw address, OpenBSD reaches the same device through the big window, so both paths have to work. See docs/datasheets/address-map.md for the small-window-0 reversal history.

machine.name: Onyx2 deskside with one InfiniteReality pipe
machine.notes: Selected installation of two node boards, each with two processors and one 64 MiB bank, joined by the midplane's Null Router. IO1 holds a BaseIO-G with its MediaIO daughtercard; the graphics board set takes XIO4 directly, with a geometry board, one raster manager with texture memory and a display generator, and no Ktown, so the pipe's one-wire chain answers the geometry record alone. The other XIO slots are empty. This is a selected population, not a captured machine inventory. The full processor mode word is not the full CP0 Config register; only the reviewed low 25 bits transfer. Stock image configuration must agree and is never rewritten by descriptor generation.

space_selection.notes: Two bits the processor drives beside the address, not part of it. All four spaces decode to the same 40-bit physical address and the attribute is what tells them apart.
